olereader

olereader reads Microsoft compound files, also called OLE2 or structured storage files, in pure R. A compound file works like a small file system inside a single file: storages act as folders and streams hold the data. Older Office documents (.doc, .xls, .ppt), Outlook messages (.msg) and many instrument and application formats use this container.

olereader lists the streams in a file, reads them into raw vectors and extracts them to disk. It has no dependencies beyond base R and does not write compound files.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ethanbass/olereader")

or install a binary from R-universe:

install.packages("olereader",
                 repos = c("https://ethanbass.r-universe.dev",
                           "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

Usage

ole_open() reads a file’s header and directory. Stream contents are only read when you ask for them.

library(olereader)

ole <- ole_open(system.file("extdata", "example.cfb", package = "olereader"))
ole
#> <ole_file> .../olereader/extdata/example.cfb
#>   version 3, 512-byte sectors, 2 streams

The other functions also take a path in place of ole, as in ole_read("file.doc", "WordDocument"). They then reopen and parse the file on every call, so use ole_open() when you read several streams.

ole_streams() lists the streams, named by their path within the file:

str(ole_streams(ole))
#> List of 2
#>  $ data        : chr "data"
#>  $ notes/readme: chr [1:2] "notes" "readme"

ole_read() returns a stream as a raw vector, which you can decode with readBin() or rawToChar(). Give the path as a vector of names or as one string separated by /. Names match ignoring the case of the letters A to Z.

ole_size(ole, "data")
#> [1] 5000

rawToChar(ole_read(ole, c("notes", "readme")))
#> [1] "This is the readme stream of the olereader example file. It is short enough to be in the mini stream."

ole_extract() writes streams to files, with one folder for each storage. It extracts every stream by default, or only the ones you name in streams:

ole_extract(ole, "example")
list.files("example", recursive = TRUE)
#> [1] "data"         "notes/readme"

ole_extract(ole, "example", streams = "notes/readme", overwrite = TRUE)

Format

olereader is written from Microsoft’s MS-CFB specification. It reads version 3 (512-byte sectors) and version 4 (4096-byte sectors) files. ole_streams() lists streams in the same order as listdir() in the Python package olefile, and dev/compare_olefile.R in the source repository checks that the two packages return the same streams, sizes and bytes for any files you give it.

Logo

The logo shows the dancer Pepita de Oliva, from the cover of the sheet music El olé (Vienna: H. F. Müller’s Witwe, 1850s), held by the New York Public Library’s Jerome Robbins Dance Division. The print is in the public domain.
